templates.name: Ticket classifier
templates.description: Classifies a support ticket into one of a fixed set of labels, with a short justification.

prompt.title: Ticket classifier — structured JSON
prompt.purpose: Route support tickets to the right queue. One of a fixed set of labels, plus a short justification so reviewers can audit decisions.
prompt.body:
You are a careful support-ticket triage assistant.

Classify the ticket below into exactly one of these labels:
  billing · account · product · other

Respond with a single JSON object on one line, no prose:
  {"label": "<one of the labels>", "justification": "<≤ 20 words>"}

Ticket:
{{ticket}}

variables.name: ticket
variables.description: The raw ticket body to classify.

prompt.readme:
## Ticket classifier

**Contract**
- Input: raw ticket body under `{{ticket}}`.
- Output: one-line JSON with `label` ∈ {billing, account, product, other} and a ≤ 20-word `justification`.
- Ambiguity: return `"other"` and explain why.

**Shipping policy**
Regress every change against `billing`, `account`, and `other` examples before promoting.

**Known edge cases**
- Refund requests without an order number are `billing`.
- Password resets are `account`.
- Feature requests are `other`.

bindings.ticket: I was charged twice for my subscription this month. Please refund one.
I can't log in. Reset link never arrives.
Please add dark mode to the iOS app.

templates.name: Structured extractor
templates.description: Extracts a typed record from free-form text. Returns JSON matching a fixed schema, or a single error field.

prompt.title: Structured extractor — schema-constrained
prompt.purpose: Turn free-form text into a typed record. Fail loudly with a single `error` field when the input doesn't match the schema.
prompt.readme:
## Structured extractor

**Contract**
- Success: one JSON object matching the schema.
- Failure: one JSON object with a single `error` field.
- Never mix the two; never emit code fences.

**Shipping policy**
Add a schema test to the eval bundle for every new field before promoting.

bindings.text: Hi, I'm Sara Lee from Acme Corp (sara@acme.co). We'd love to see a demo.

templates.name: Chain-of-thought solver
templates.description: Solves a math or logic problem with explicit step-by-step reasoning, then emits a final answer line.

prompt.title: Chain-of-thought solver
prompt.purpose: Keep the reasoning transparent so reviewers can see why the answer is what it is.
prompt.body:
You are a careful mathematician.

Solve the problem below. Show your reasoning in short numbered steps (maximum 6). Then emit a line of exactly the form:

  ANSWER: <the final numeric or boolean answer, with no units and no punctuation>

Problem:
{{problem}}
prompt.readme:
## Chain-of-thought solver

Reasoning is visible on purpose. The `ANSWER:` line is the single machine-readable output — the rest is for humans auditing the chain.

bindings.problem: A train leaves at 2pm going 60 mph. A second train leaves at 3pm going 80 mph on the same track. When does the second train catch up?

templates.name: Code-diff reviewer
templates.description: Reviews a code diff for likely bugs, style issues, and missing tests. Returns a structured review.

prompt.title: Code-diff reviewer
prompt.purpose: Catch the obvious class of bugs (off-by-one, resource leaks, missing null checks) on small diffs before a human review.

variables.name: language
variables.description: The language of the diff, e.g. 'TypeScript'.

prompt.readme:
## Code-diff reviewer

Scope is intentionally narrow: one file, one diff. Use **blocker** sparingly — anything blocker should prevent merge.

bindings.diff:
--- a/sum.ts
+++ b/sum.ts
@@
-for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i++)
+for (let i = 0; i <= arr.length; i++)

templates.name: Bullet-point summarizer
templates.description: Condenses long prose into at most five bullet points, each ≤ 18 words. Preserves specific numbers.

prompt.title: Bullet-point summarizer
prompt.purpose: Short-form summaries for status reports and standups. Specific numbers are preserved verbatim.
prompt.body:
Summarize the document below in AT MOST five bullet points.

Rules:
  - Each bullet ≤ 18 words.
  - Preserve specific numbers, dates, and proper nouns verbatim.
  - No preamble, no conclusion.

Document:
{{document}}
prompt.readme:
## Bullet-point summarizer

The 18-word ceiling is load-bearing — it forces the model to drop filler. Tune it before shipping.

bindings.document: In Q1 2026, revenue grew 14% year-over-year to $42.1M. Paid seats crossed 10,000 for the first time. Churn held at 2.3% monthly. We opened an office in Berlin.

templates.name: Rubric-based judge
templates.description: Scores a candidate answer against a rubric. Emits per-criterion scores + a short rationale.

prompt.title: Rubric-based judge
prompt.purpose: Produce per-criterion scores that a human reviewer can audit. Never a single opaque score.
prompt.readme:
## Rubric-based judge

The rationale field is mandatory. A judge that can't explain its scores is a black box.
